Hi Claire — quick technical note ahead of the deep-dive. Short answers first: yes, the local emulator covers schema validation + a predictable routing layer; you can run end-to-end without sending any production traffic to the hosted API.

Practical local bootstrap (high-level):
1) Clone sample repo (see Drive/Git link)
2) Create .env.dev from .env.example and set: REDWOOD_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 (emulator), REDWOOD_API_KEY=dev-<placeholder>, REDWOOD_MODEL_ALIAS=text-search-small
3) Python: pip install -r requirements.txt; run python app/search_local.py --dataset sample-data.json
4) TypeScript: npm ci; npm run start:local (process listens on 3000 and shows structured output validations)
5) To test tool-calling / function outputs: run the demo runner with --simulate-tools flag (the emulator will return predictable tool responses for schema tests)

Routing and structured output notes:
- You can declare route maps in routes.yaml (example in repo) to send short queries to cheaper small models and long-running parses to a larger variant. Router supports model_alias + region + fallback chains.
- Structured output: schema-first enforcement is available via the SDK's expect_schema(json_schema) wrapper; the emulator will reject outputs that don't conform so you can build unit tests around it.

Embeddings & reranker guidance:
- For your search size (~500k docs), start with 1536-d embeddings, shard index every ~50k documents; our sample provides a local FAISS index builder script
- Reranker: use two-step scoring (embedding recall -> reranker neural score) to keep latency flat; we include a light Python reranker example in the repo

Security / KMS / retention:
- The local emulator never persists RGW; for pilot hosted runs we can provide a short security pack (SOC2 summary + audit log samples). For KMS integration we provide a pattern doc and a sample env var set (KMS_KEY_ID=proj-horton-dev) — actual key provisioning will be in Private path or Dedicated depending on contract

I'll run through the routes.yaml + schema enforcement in the deep-dive. Attached to this message: a short checklist and an example routes.yaml (also included in the repo archive).

Cheers,
